body:
For you: nothing to do. When a part crashes, the orchestrator now relaunches it on its own branch and tells it to continue from the checklist in its post. It asks you only when the step was waiting on your answer.

## What changed
- **Parts checkpoint.** The part prompts (CLI, web, agy) now say: your post is your task list. Its pieces (`kit.py sub <post> "<piece>" --status doing|done`) show what is done, what is in progress and what is next. At the end of each piece, and before any long command, run `kit.py checkpoint <post>`: a WIP commit on the part's branch, pushed, with the post stamped `checkpoint: {branch, sha, at, pushed}`. It refuses to run on the trunk, as before.
- **resume lists stopped steps.** Under each in-progress step whose session is not running, resume shows its branch, its last checkpoint, `checklist 1/3 done · doing: 2. ... · next: 3. ...`, and `relaunch: python3 -I .kit/kit.py launch <post> --continue`. When the transcript is still on this machine it also shows `claude --resume <id>`. A web session gets the same lines, marked 'once its session is confirmed ended'.
- **`launch --continue`.** On the CLI it reuses the old worktree as it was left, uncommitted files included. If that worktree is gone it checks out the branch, from origin if needed, and never resets it. On the web, create_session clones the part's branch. The prompt adds: continue from the checklist in your post (next: ...); your branch has your work (last checkpoint ...). It refuses when the session still runs or the step waits on the owner (column question/todo, a waiting status, or an open question naming the part). The post records `relaunched {at, from, n}`.
- **The orchestrator relaunches without asking**, inside the device cap: resume's closing line and both orchestrator prompts (CLI, web) now say so.

## What I checked
The kill test (`tests/test_cl17_crash_continue.py`): a fake `claude --bg` starts a real process. The part writes parser.py, marks piece 1 done and piece 2 in progress, checkpoints, then writes cli.py and is killed with SIGKILL. Its worktree and branch are deleted, so only origin has the work. resume then shows the checkpoint, the checklist and the relaunch line. `launch --continue` starts at the checkpoint commit, with parser.py present and cli.py gone, and its prompt names piece 2. Other tests cover: a running part is not relaunched, a step waiting on the owner is not relaunched, and a checkpoint on main is refused.

The test fails on the old kit.py (5 errors). One existing control test (`tests/test_resume_attached_boards.py`) compares resume's closing line byte for byte, so it now swaps CL17's new sentence for the old one before comparing.

Full suite: 81 of 81 suites pass after merging main, with the real board server running. That run exposed a latent leak: three test files (mine, test_launch, test_cl49) read the real board on port 8765 whenever it ran. The cause was kit.py reading posts from the config's board_url ahead of KIT_BOARD_URL. Fixed in kit.py (the environment variable now wins), plus the two launch tests' own configs.

Not checked: see the field. On this web session, the artifact reconcile wanted to push 328 unpinned writes because my first pull covered only my own post. I did not send them, so the orchestrator's next full pull or reconcile carries the board. Then the kit's guard refused every read (list or get) while a push batch was out, even after I moved the batches aside. A part on the web whose first pull was partial cannot get its post onto the Artifact on its own. This post is in the local copy and in git (board-mirror via the save). The orchestrator should send it, and the guard needs a fix (a new step).
handoff: Parts now checkpoint with `kit.py checkpoint <post>` and keep their checklist as post pieces (`kit.py sub`). The orchestrator relaunches a stopped step with `kit.py launch <post> --continue`, inside the device cap, and asks only when the step waits on the owner. CL8/9/10/12/14: their old work is in uncommitted worktrees, which `--continue` reuses when the worktree is still on this machine.
not_checked: a real Claude Code crash (OOM, closed laptop): the test kills a stand-in process in place of `claude --bg`
the web path: `launch --continue` puts the part's branch in create_session's source_revision, but no real cloud session was started
agy: its orchestrator still continues a part with invoke_subagent. The relaunch line is `kit.py launch`, which needs `claude`
`claude --resume <id>` is offered only when the post's session_id is a UUID whose transcript exists here; a `--bg -n <name>` session is not mapped to its transcript

title: A crashed part is continued from its last checkpoint
verdict: A part that crashes now carries on from its last save. Its post keeps its to-do list, GitHub keeps its work, and the orchestrator restarts it there on its own, asking you only when the part was waiting on your answer.
